subject.title: [Feature]: When messages are merged and processed, the agent event is expected to carry the original runId(s)

question: Should merged queued Gateway events preserve the executed `runId` and add an original/source run ID array, or should merged execution reuse one of the queued source run IDs as the public run ID?
rationale: Current code can track queued identities internally, but the public Gateway event contract is stable and the issue proposes two different API semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Add additive lineage array
options.body: Preserve the executed `runId` and add a named array such as `originalRunIds` or `sourceRunIds` to public event schemas and projections.

options.title: Reuse a source run ID
options.body: Make merged execution appear under the first or last queued source ID, which helps simple clients but hides multi-source lineage and changes run identity semantics.

options.title: Keep the current contract
options.body: Leave clients to correlate through accepted/final events and history, accepting that merged queued execution cannot be mapped one-to-one from live agent events.

recommendation.title: Add additive lineage array
recommendation.body: Preserve the executed `runId` and add a named array such as `originalRunIds` or `sourceRunIds` to public event schemas and projections.

likelyOwner.reason: The current protocol/event lines and Gateway projection history most strongly route this API-shape decision to `steipete`.
